rules: Unresolved is a first-class result; "no trout" is a strong exclusion claim requiring scoped positive evidence.
Warmwater focus is a positive claim and may coexist with seasonal trout.
A reservoir is a trout fishery, not a trout stream; lake arms/depth never inherit tailwater evidence.
A stocking schedule is a plan; the recent-release report is a rolling window; a GIS point is neither.
Designations (TS/NRTS) are legal boundaries, never a fish census.

waters.name: Barren Fork River

catalogFields.notes: TWRA spring-stocked Warren County river through McMinnville. Gentle gradient; flows track rain closely.

headline.statement: TWRA's 2026 schedule puts this Warren County water on a spring put-and-take program (rainbow trout stocked the weeks of Mar 15, Mar 22 and May 10, 2026); it is a scheduled stocking program with a spring stocking window, not a documented year-round fishery.

source.title: 2026 Trout Stocking Schedule (published table)
source.pinpoint: 3 rows: LOCATION 'Barren Fork River', COUNTY Warren, REGION 3, TYPE Seasonal, Rainbow Trout, weeks 3/15, 3/22, 5/10/2026

claims.statement: TWRA schedules three 2026 spring rainbow stockings on the Barren Fork River (Warren Co.), all Seasonal type; the program window implied by the rows is March-May.
claims.qualification: "Week of" schedule dates are Sundays; TWRA states each stocking event occurs within five days after the listed date and can be postponed or cancelled (e.g., adverse weather or warm water). Stocking weeks are the program's own declared months for this water; they are not a guaranteed fishing window and no agency document states a fishing season for this water.

source.title: TWRA Trout Stocking Locations layer (GIS points, no dates)
source.method: stocking-location layer (points are neither events nor complete stocked reaches)

claims.statement: The TWRA stocking-location layer lists one Spring rainbow point on this water: 'Pepper Branch Park (S1)', Warren County, stream class.
claims.qualification: A GIS point marks a mapped stocking access, not a completed release and not the limit of the stocked reach.

qualifications: Spring put-and-take program only: TWRA's Trout Management Plan 2017-2027 describes hatchery-supported waters like this as primarily warmwater habitats that cannot support trout year round (plan program text re-verified first-hand this pass for the program generally, not for this water specifically).
The 'N Barren Fork Creek' rows in the same schedule are a different water (North Prong Barren Fork, separately cataloged) and were correctly excluded from this join.
No holdover or wild-trout documentation exists for this water; do not assume stocked fish persist between or after stockings.

priorLeads.segment: The Barren Fork River, Warren County, flowing through McMinnville to its confluence with the Collins River just north of McMinnville (the Barren Fork lies inside the Collins HUC-8 05130107). TWRA's stocked reach is the Warren County main stem; the cataloged North Prong Barren Fork is cataloged separately (north-prong-barren-fork).
priorLeads.boundaries: Warren County main stem through McMinnville; HUC 05130107. Temperature evidence: TDEC stations at river-miles 4.4, 15.2, and 16.4 (35.63-35.68 N, the McMinnville reach) and USGS 03420500 near Trousdale.

coldSourceSummary.notes: No cold-water source documented. Catalog describes a gentle-gradient rain-driven river through McMinnville - no dam, no spring source cited by any agency.

holdover.detail: No agency documentation of holdover either way. TWRA's stocking is seasonal (three 2026 weeks: 3/15, 3/22, 5/10, Rainbow Trout); no summer/winter stocking rows and no creel or sampling evidence of between-stocking survival were found.

wildPopulation.detail: No wild trout documented: the Barren Fork appears in NO TWRA trout category - the wild-trout list and every other trout designation on TWRA's trout regulations page exclude it (checked live this session), so the agency trout record here is stocking-based put-and-take rainbow only. (Wave-2's audit 'wild-trout candidate' flag was refuted at page level; a stocking program is not a wild-trout designation.)

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: TDEC's 2007-2008 sampling on the McMinnville reach shows summer water of 20-26.8 C (26.8 C in Aug 2007 at river-mile 4.4) and TWRA stocks the Barren Fork only in three spring weeks - seasonal put-and-take rainbow with no documented between-stocking survival.

waters.name: Beaverdam Creek

catalogFields.notes: Johnson County spring creek with cold, steady water and TWRA spring stocking; a favorite small-water rainbow stop on the Shatley Springs road corridor. The reach from the Birch Branch confluence down to Tank Hollow Road is a designated TWRA wild-trout water — open year-round, single-hook artificials only. No USGS gauge — plan on recent-rain judgment.

headline.reachScope: Designated wild-trout reach (Birch Branch confluence downstream to Tank Hollow Rd/USFS 300) for the year-round wild fishery; the hatchery-supported spring stocking (Mar-Jun) applies to the stocked reach
headline.statement: A documented year-round trout water: TWRA designates the Birch Branch-to-Tank Hollow reach a wild trout water and TWRA's in-force Trout Management Plan says Beaverdam Creek today 'provide[s] excellent wild trout fisheries'; a seasonal spring rainbow stocking (Mar-Jun 2026) coexists with the wild fishery.

source.title: Tennessee Trout Regulations

claims.statement: TWRA's trout regulations list 'Beaverdam Creek and tributaries from its confluence with Birch Branch downstream to Tank Hollow Road' (Johnson Co.) on the Wild Trout Streams list; the same entry is confirmed verbatim on the eRegulations publisher copy.
claims.qualification: The designation is reach-specific: year-round wild-trout management applies to the named reach, not necessarily the lowest creek toward the Virginia line.

source.title: Tennessee Trout Management Plan 2017-2027
source.pinpoint: wild-trout chapter: "several of Tennessee's larger coldwater streams including Beaverdam Creek, Doe Creek, and Tellico River had poor water quality... Today, these streams, along with many others, provide excellent wild trout fisheries."

claims.statement: TWRA's in-force statewide plan documents Beaverdam Creek as a water that today provides an excellent wild trout fishery; combined with the current wild-trout designation (no seasonal closure listed for it on the trout regulations page) this supports a year-round trout opportunity on the designated reach.
claims.qualification: A wild trout fishery is a resident population, i.e., trout present all year; the year-round open-season inference rests on TWRA listing no closure for this water (closures elsewhere are listed as explicit exceptions).

source.title: 2026 Trout Stocking Schedule (published table)
source.pinpoint: 5 rows: 'Beaverdam Creek', Johnson Co., REGION 4, Seasonal, Rainbow Trout, weeks 3/1, 3/29, 4/26, 5/24, 6/21/2026

claims.statement: TWRA additionally schedules five 2026 spring rainbow stockings (Mar-Jun) on Beaverdam Creek, Johnson County.
claims.qualification: "Week of" schedule dates are Sundays; TWRA states each stocking event occurs within five days after the listed date and can be postponed or cancelled (e.g., adverse weather or warm water). Stocking and wild fish coexist; stocked-fish presence is seasonal even though the wild fishery is year-round.

claims.qualification: Prior research lead, not re-verified: the repository full text is bot-blocked (HTTP 403) this pass; only the landing-page title/year was confirmed. Currency of the 2018 assessment is not established.

qualifications: Reach discipline: the year-round claim is anchored on the designated wild-trout reach (Birch Branch confluence to Tank Hollow Rd); conditions on the lowest private reaches toward the state line are not separately documented.
The catalog note's regulation summary (single-hook artificials on the wild reach) was not re-verified this pass; confirm current rules with TWRA before you go.

priorLeads.segment: Beaverdam Creek, Johnson County — northeast Tennessee spring-creek-character creek in the Watauga HUC (06010102, South Fork Holston basin), flowing through Cherokee National Forest country toward the Virginia line near Damascus. TWRA Region IV report treats it as an annually monitored wild trout stream.
priorLeads.boundaries: Wild-trout water: 'Beaverdam Creek and tributaries from its confluence with Birch Branch downstream to Tank Hollow' (TWRA special trout regulations, wild trout streams table) — 5 trout/day, no length limit, single-hook artificials only. Reaches outside that designation: statewide trout rules. TWRA 2026 stocking schedule lists seasonal rainbow stocking weeks 3/1-6/21/2026 (every 4 weeks).

coldSourceSummary.notes: Catalog calls it a spring creek but no agency text confirming spring influence was found. Elevation context from TWRA Trout Management Plan: a 2006 qualitative survey of Green Mountain Branch (a Beaverdam Creek tributary) found a relatively abundant wild Rainbow Trout population at 3,080 ft elevation along Hwy 421 (https://digitalcommons.memphis.edu/govpubs-tn-wra-strategic-management-plans/10).

holdover.detail: No holdover-specific evidence found. Decisive currency is the documented resident wild trout population (below); TWRA 2026 seasonal rainbow stocking (Mar-Jun) coexists with the wild fishery.

wildPopulation.detail: TWRA Region IV Trout Fisheries Report 2018: 'Beaverdam Creek is one of Tennessee's best-known wild trout streams and is on an annual monitoring schedule' — monitored since 1991 with primary species RBT/BNT; qualitative surveys found RBT and BNT at mainstem sites. Brook trout documented in Beaverdam Creek tributaries (Birch Branch listed among sympatric Brook/Rainbow waters; East Fork Beaverdam Creek listed as a potential native Brook Trout donor stream) — tributary evidence, not mainstem. TWRA Trout Management Plan 2017-2027 names Beaverdam Creek among former degraded streams that now 'provide excellent wild trout fisheries'.

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: TWRA itself calls Beaverdam Creek one of Tennessee's best-known wild trout streams, annually monitored since 1991 for resident rainbow and brown trout — a self-sustaining population in a designated wild-trout water.

waters.name: Beech Lake

catalogFields.notes: TWRA winter put-and-take lake in Lexington (Henderson County). Stocked with rainbow trout in the cold months only — the fish do not hold over summer. Check the TWRA schedule for the current winter window before you go.

headline.statement: Winter put-and-take rainbow program on Beech Lake at Lexington (Henderson Co.): TWRA's 2026 schedule lists a Winter stocking on Jan 14, 2026 and the next one TBD Dec 2026 - a cold-month program, not a year-round trout fishery.

source.title: 2026 Trout Stocking Schedule (published table)
source.pinpoint: 2 rows: 'Beech Lake', Henderson Co., REGION 1, TYPE Winter, Rainbow Trout, days 1/14/2026 and 'TBD 12/2026'

claims.statement: TWRA's winter trout program stocks Beech Lake with rainbow trout in the cold months; the 2026 schedule carries exactly two Winter rows (mid-Jan 2026 and a to-be-announced Dec 2026 event).
claims.qualification: "Week of" schedule dates are Sundays; TWRA states each stocking event occurs within five days after the listed date and can be postponed or cancelled (e.g., adverse weather or warm water). The window is the winter program's own schedule for this water; no year-round trout presence is implied.

source.title: TWRA Trout Stocking Locations layer (GIS points, no dates)
source.method: stocking-location layer (points are neither events nor complete stocked reaches)

claims.statement: The stocking-location layer lists 'Beech Lake' (Lexington, HENDERSON Co., pond class, Winter program, rainbow, ~1,500 fish).
claims.qualification: Point counts and NumStocked values are planning figures, not event records.

qualifications: Winter program design: TWRA's Trout Management Plan (Winter Trout Program section, verified first-hand this pass) says the program 'provides trout angling opportunity during the winter months' and describes hatchery-supported lakes as primarily warmwater habitats that cannot support trout year round; do not expect a documented summer trout fishery, but absence after winter is not biologically proven either.
Underlying fishery is warmwater (bass/bream-type lake per program context); a positive warmwater assemblage document was not verified for this lake this pass.
Daily creel is 7 trout statewide (5 at Community Lakes Fishing Program locations); a trout license is needed in addition to the fishing license.

meanings: winter put-and-take on a warm water (cold-month recruitment program)

priorLeads.segment: Beech Lake (USGS/TVA 'Beech Reservoir') on the Beech River at Lexington, Henderson County, West Tennessee. TWRA Region 1 winter put-and-take trout lake (catalog: seasonMonths Nov-Mar) over a warmwater bass/bream/catfish fishery; one of the 'Beech River Watershed Lakes' group in TWRA's regulation exceptions.
priorLeads.boundaries: Entire lake. TWRA's 2026 trout stocking schedule lists 'Beech Lake' as a Winter-type Rainbow Trout site (repo workbook rows: Henderson Co., 1/14/2026 and TBD 12/2026; the schedule page renders dates 1/13/2026 and 2/10/2026 adjacent to the Beech Lake entry). No trout stockings of any other type found for the lake.

coldSourceSummary.notes: Dam identity basis: USGS inactive station 03594413 is named 'BEECH LAKE NEAR LEXINGTON, TENN (TVA)' (Henderson Co., HUC 06040001 Lower Tennessee-Beech, 35.66118,-88.41727). TVA's 'Beech Reservoir' page (tva.com, verified via WebSearch snippet only — tva.com blocks plain fetch) describes flood-storage of 4,430 acre-feet, ~3.65 miles long, and Beech Dam as a non-hydro dam; a WebSearch synthesis adds the dam was built early 1960s for water supply/flood control/recreation. No cold-release (deep-draw) regime documented; no evidence the lake receives or needs cold dam water.

holdover.detail: No site-specific holdover evidence found. Program design is winter put-and-take: the only trout rows for Beech Lake in TWRA's 2026 schedule are Winter-type, and the TWRA Trout Management Plan 2017-2027 states hatchery-supported streams and lakes 'are primarily warmwater habitats that cannot support trout year round'. Warmwater stockings (bluegill/redear) also appear for the lake in TWRA's warmwater stocking archive.

wildPopulation.detail: No wild trout presence documented. The Trout Management Plan states wild trout are generally limited to East Tennessee's mountain streams; no wild-trout listing or record exists for this West Tennessee reservoir.

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: Winter put-and-take only: TWRA's 2026 schedule carries Beech Lake (Henderson Co.) solely as a Winter rainbow site, and the Trout Management Plan states hatchery-supported lakes like this are warmwater habitats that cannot support trout year round.

priorLeads.segment: Big Rock Creek, Marshall County, Tennessee (catalog) — a small Duck River tributary through Lewisburg, rising in southwest Marshall County and flowing north about 20 river miles to its confluence with the Duck River (TDEC's nearest mainstem station is described as 'HIGHWAY 272 DOWNSTEAM BIG ROCK CREEK' at 35.577, -86.779, HUC 06040002). Catalog YAML carries no counties field; identity resolved from the catalog hydroIdentity (GNIS 01305230, HUC8 06040002) and confirmed against WQP station metadata: every 'Big Rock Creek' station found sits in HUC 06040002 with county code 117 (Marshall), matching the catalog note 'TWRA winter-stocked Marshall County creek near Lewisburg'. Same-named Big Rock Creeks elsewhere in Tennessee were not an issue here — all stations returned by the Marshall County sweep belong to this creek.
priorLeads.boundaries: The named Big Rock Creek within Marshall County (HUC 06040002); identity stations USGS-03599000 'BIG ROCK CREEK AT LEWISBURG, TN' (24.9 sq mi, alt 705.01 ft NGVD29) and USGS-03599100 'BIG ROCK CR AT DOUBLE BRIDGES, TN' (48.7 sq mi, alt 644.37 ft). TWRA's stocking-site string is 'Big Rock Greenway' (Region 2, Marshall) with no reach detail; the greenway lies along the creek in Lewisburg, so in-town gauge USGS-03599000 is the nearest temperature station to the stocking site.

coldSourceSummary.notes: Elevation 705.01 ft is the USGS-03599000 station altitude at Lewisburg (NGVD29); the downstream Double Bridges station sits at 644.37 ft — a low-relief agricultural/urban Marshall County valley with no gorge or canopy documentation found. No cold-water source of any kind documented. TDEC station TDECWPC-BROCK006.0ML is described as '100 YARDS DOWNSTREAM DAM AT VERONA', evidencing an unnamed small dam on the creek at Verona; no operator or release documentation exists, and the 26.3 deg C July 2000 grab below it shows no cold-release effect. Identity verified from WQP station metadata columns (station names, Marshall County code 117, HUC 06040002) because the USGS identity endpoint has been 503ing this week.

holdover.detail: No holdover documentation found. The TWRA program is winter-only catchable rainbows at 'Big Rock Greenway': 2026 workbook rows (Region 2, Marshall, type Winter, Rainbow Trout) are 1/15/2026, 2/27/2026 and TBD 12/2026; the live TWRA stocking page contains the 'Big Rock Greenway' site string (fetched copy's flattened table interleaves two tables, so its stray date cells cannot be attributed). No source documents survival between stockings or through summer, and the in-town summer record (USGS-03599000 nearest the greenway: 24.7-32.0 deg C June-September grabs) makes summer survival implausible on the cited temperatures alone.

wildPopulation.detail: No wild trout documentation found in any agency source for Big Rock Creek. TWRA's Trout Management Plan 2017-2027 places Tennessee's wild trout in East Tennessee and describes hatchery-supported streams and lakes as 'primarily warmwater habitats that cannot support trout year round' (canon quote; PDF not fetched per rule).

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: 91 June-September grab samples across 1966-2025 on every reach of Big Rock Creek run 18.5-32.0 deg C — 25.3-32.0 deg C at the in-town Lewisburg gauge nearest the Big Rock Greenway stocking site — far above year-round trout survival thresholds.

waters.name: Boone Lake

catalogFields.notes:
TVA reservoir on the South Fork Holston River northeast of Johnson City (Sullivan/Washington counties), impounded by Boone Dam (USGS 03486810, 36.44066/-82.43792). Two arms: the South Fork Holston arm fed by the South Holston Dam tailwater (south-holston-river) and the Watauga arm fed by the Wilbur Dam tailwater (watauga-river). Outflow is the Boone tailwater (boone-tailwater) down to Fort Patrick Henry Lake. Aliases: Boone Reservoir. TWRA's Boone Reservoir page lists the fishery as largemouth bass, smallmouth bass, spotted bass, crappie, bluegill, catfish, striped bass (see officialSources).
Striped bass is a regulatory or hybrid-evidence tag here; reservoir temperature/oxygen refuge context is not a scored input.

Regulations: LMB/SMB 5/day combined, 15" min; spotted bass 15/day no limit; crappie 15/day combined 10" min; striped/hybrid 2/day combined (1 striped max; 36" min striped, 15" min hybrid); (retrieved 2026-09-14; verify current rules with TWRA before you go).

priorLeads.segment: Buffalo Creek in Grainger County, Tennessee — the TWRA-stocked trout stream near Rutledge and Tampico that runs through Buffalo Springs WMA (TWRA's 342-acre WMA with the Buffalo Springs trout hatchery on site). Explicitly a different stream from Buffalo Creek at Norris in Anderson County (USGS 03534500), as the catalog notes.
priorLeads.boundaries: TWRA regulation exceptions treat 'Buffalo Creek (and tributaries) within the WMA boundary, Grainger County' as one unit: from the mill dam upstream is closed year-round to all fishing; from the mill dam downstream is open year-round to rod-and-reel fishing. Temperature evidence cited here is from the TDEC monitoring point at the Tamipco Road bridge (36.1941,-83.5627), the same reach USGS lists as 'BUFFALO CREEK AT TAMPICO, TN' (USGS 03494530, HUC 06010104, Grainger County).

coldSourceSummary.notes: No dam on the stocked reach. TWRA's Buffalo Springs WMA page (Grainger County) places a fish hatchery on the WMA and describes Buffalo Creek itself as accessible along the WMA dirt road; the WMA sits ~1 km upstream of the Tampico gauge point, tying the stocked creek to the same watershed as the temperature record. The catchment is a ~19.6 sq mi lowland Grainger County basin (USGS 03494528 'BUFFALO CREEK NR TAMPICO' drainage area); no gorge, gradient, or canopy description found on an agency page.

holdover.detail: No site-specific holdover survey exists. The program structure itself documents multi-month carry-over of stocked fish: TWRA's exceptions text sets a Delayed Harvest season on Buffalo Creek (WMA boundary reach) from Oct 1 to Jan 31 with catch-and-release and artificial lures only, i.e., fall-stocked trout must survive in-stream for months to be available to the Feb 1-Sept 30 harvest season that follows.

wildPopulation.detail: No wild trout listing or natural-reproduction documentation found for Buffalo Creek (Grainger). The TWRA Trout Management Plan 2017-2027 treats wild trout as an East Tennessee mountain/tailwater phenomenon and lists hatchery-supported streams as warmwater habitats; Buffalo Creek appears only as a stocked stream, and all workbook stocking rows are hatchery rainbow trout. (Name collision note: TWRA's Buffalo Springs HATCHERY is on this WMA — 'Buffalo' there refers to the spring/hatchery, not a wild trout stream.)

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: TDEC grab samples at the Tamipco Road bridge show summer water of only 15.5-19.2 C across 2010-2025 (12 Jun-Sep observations, max 19.16 C in Jul 2024), and TWRA stocks the creek weekly from February through August plus an Oct 1-Jan 31 delayed-harvest catch-and-release season — near-year-round trout presence both measured and programmatic.

waters.name: Calderwood Lake

catalogFields.notes:
Small reservoir on the Little Tennessee River along the North Carolina line in Blount County, impounded by Calderwood Dam. Receives Little Tennessee flow from Fontana Lake (NC) and discharges into Chilhowee Lake. TWRA stocks the reservoir with rainbow trout in November and December. TWRA lists this pool as "Little Calderwood Reservoir" (458 ac) — that name is an alias here. TWRA's Calderwood Reservoir page lists the fishery as largemouth bass, smallmouth bass, crappie, bluegill, catfish (see officialSources).

Regulations: Trout 7/day, no length limit, only 2 may be lake trout; black bass 5/day combined, only 2 under 14"; crappie 20/day combined 8" min; white bass 10/day 14" min; sauger 8/day 15" min; muskellunge 1/day 42" min; walleye 8/day no limit; (retrieved 2026-09-14; verify current rules with TWRA before you go).

Cataloged with USGS gauge 03419530 (Calfkiller River at Hwy 70 at Sparta); TWRA's stocked reach is the White County river.
priorLeads.boundaries: County spread: White (GNIS 01305600; the cataloged river), headwaters in Putnam; HUC 05130108. Temperature evidence below comes from stations at/below Sparta on the lower-mid river.

coldSourceSummary.notes: No cold-water source documented. The catalog's 'spring-fed-ish' characterization is an editorial note without an agency citation. TWRA's Great Falls Reservoir page documents the river's lower reach as musky habitat whose fishing 'is tough [a]s water temperatures rise during the summer' - a warmwater signal for the lower river.

holdover.detail: No agency documentation of holdover either way. TWRA stocks the river only in spring (two seasonal 2026 weeks of 3/22 and 3/29, Rainbow Trout); no summer or winter stocking rows exist, and no creel or sampling evidence of between-stocking survival was found.

wildPopulation.detail: No wild trout documented: the Calfkiller appears in no TWRA trout-regulation category (absent from the wild-trout list and every special-regulation section of TWRA's trout regulations page, checked live this session); the musky/bass fishery TWRA documents for the river's lower reach is warmwater.

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: TWRA stocks the Calfkiller only in spring (2 seasonal rainbow weeks in March 2026) and grab samples below Sparta show summer water up to 29.0 C (Jul 1980), with 21.8-25 C typical - warmwater summer conditions with no documented between-stocking survival.

priorLeads.boundaries: Center Hill Dam down to the Cumberland River confluence; stocking and study reach is the first 26 km below the dam; Stonewall gauge reach

coldSourceSummary.notes: USACE Nashville District project; the reservoir is thermally stratified and hypolimnial release drives tailwater temperature (Devlin & Bettoli 1999, Proc. SEAFWA 53:100-109, https://seafwa.org/sites/default/files/journal-articles/DEVLIN-100-109.pdf). In June 2024 USACE reinstalled a ~120-ft-deep orifice gate establishing a 250 cfs summer/fall minimum continuous flow specifically to 'mitigat[e] the risk of elevated temperatures' and support the 'renowned cold-water trout fishery' (USACE-affiliated account). PEER report 'Last Gasp' documents historical summer/fall low-flow DO problems (https://peer.org/wp-content/uploads/attachments/05_23_8_centerhilldam.pdf). Temperature: generation-period tailwater temperatures ranged 9-19 C across 1997, the warmest at November fall turnover (Devlin & Bettoli 1999); no summer-month-attributed numeric reading is stated in that study - hence empty summerTemperature. USGS 03424860 (Caney Fork at Stonewall) is confirmed the correct tailwater-reach gauge but carries no temperature parameter (checked via https://waterservices.usgs.gov/nwis/iv/?sites=03424860&parameterCd=00010&startDT=2025-07-01&endDT=2025-07-31&format=json).

holdover.detail: Devlin & Bettoli (1999): brown trout stocked in 1997 survived at 34% after 200 days post-stocking vs 7-14% for the three rainbow cohorts; i.e., stocked browns persist through summer and beyond in the tailwater.

wildPopulation.detail: No confirmed natural-reproduction anchor found in this pass. The Devlin & Bettoli (1999) study examined only stocked cohorts and reports no age-0 wild recruitment data; the fishery is managed as put-grow-take with a trophy brown program. TWRA Region IV reports may address Caney reproduction - unverified here.

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: Hypolimnial releases kept generation-period tailwater temperatures at 9-19 C through 1997 and 34% of stocked browns survived 200 days, with USACE now guaranteeing a 250 cfs cold-season minimum flow to protect the fishery.

coldSourceSummary.notes: TWRA states 'The United States Army Corps of Engineers is the operating authority of Center Hill Reservoir' (18,220 acres; DeKalb, Putnam, Warren, White counties). The bottom-draw release (~120-ft-deep orifice gate, reinstalled June 2024) describes the dam's deep discharge - it is what makes the TAILWATER below the dam cold, not the lake itself: the reservoir is thermally stratified (Devlin & Bettoli 1999 documented the stratification driving the hypolimnial tailwater release), and the one WQP surface reading at the near-dam reservoir station was 31.63 C in July 2012. TWRA's lake fishery page lists black bass, crappie, walleye, bluegill, catfish - no trout.

holdover.detail: No trout are stocked into the lake (TWRA's 2026 stocking feed has zero Center Hill LAKE rows - the only 'Center Hill' row is 'Center Hill TW / Caney Fork River', the tailwater below the dam), so no lake holdover is documented either way.

wildPopulation.detail: No wild trout documented. TWRA's reservoir page describes the fishery as black bass (largemouth/smallmouth/spotted), crappie, walleye, bluegill, catfish with detailed black-bass survey commentary and no trout mention. The lake is absent from TWRA's year-round reservoir trout stocking list (Dale Hollow, Parksville, Calderwood, Chilhowee, Fort Patrick Henry, South Holston, Tellico Upper, Watauga) verified live on TWRA's trout page this session, and absent from all trout categories on the trout regulations page.

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: The lake's surface water hit 31.63 C in July 2012 at the near-dam WQP station and TWRA manages it purely as a warmwater bass/crappie fishery with no trout stocking; whether trout could survive year-round in its cold hypolimnion is untested because TWRA has never put a trout program on the lake.

waters.name: Cherokee Lake

catalogFields.notes:
TVA reservoir on the Holston River northeast of Knoxville across Grainger, Hamblen, Hawkins, and Jefferson counties, impounded by Cherokee Dam (USGS 03493510 tailwater gauge, 36.16620/-83.49934). Receives the Holston River main stem (holston-river); its dam releases the Holston Cherokee tailwater that runs to Fort Loudoun Lake. TWRA maps the pool at 27,029 ac; TVA at 30,300 ac at full pool. TWRA's Cherokee Reservoir page lists the fishery as largemouth bass, smallmouth bass, spotted bass, crappie, bluegill, catfish, striped bass (see officialSources). Striped bass is a regulatory or hybrid-evidence tag here; reservoir temperature/oxygen refuge context is not a scored input.

Regulations: Largemouth/Smallmouth 5/day combined, Largemouth 15-in min; Smallmouth Jun 1–Oct 15 = 1/day 18-in min, Oct 16–May 31 = 5/day 15-in min; Spotted/Alabama 15/day no limit; Crappie 15/day 10-in; Striper/hybrid 2/day 15-in; Walleye/Sauger/Saugeye 10/day 15-in; (retrieved 2026-09-14; verify current rules with TWRA before you go).

headline.reachScope: Cherokee Lake (Cherokee Reservoir) pool — TVA impoundment of the Holston River across Grainger/Hamblen/Hawkins/Jefferson counties; excludes the Cherokee Dam tailwater below the dam (the stocked trout reach, catalog holston-river)
headline.statement: TWRA documents Cherokee Reservoir as a warmwater fishery with largemouth, smallmouth, striped and hybrid striped bass (locally called Cherokee bass), crappie, walleye, and saugeye. Its trout program on this system is documented below the dam, on a separate tailwater reach; lake-wide trout opportunity remains undocumented.

source.title: TWRA Cherokee Reservoir where-to-fish page
source.pinpoint: Fishery text names "Largemouth Bass, Smallmouth Bass, Striped Bass, Cherokee bass, Crappie, Walleye, and Saugeye as the primary gamefish species."; stripers "must be maintained by stocking" and "do not normally grow big in Cherokee Reservoir, due to low summer dissolved oxygen levels and high temperatures." The word "trout" appears nowhere in the fishery body (verified 2026-09-22).

claims.statement: TWRA positively documents a warmwater gamefish fishery on the reservoir; even the coldwater-adapted striped bass program is documented as marginal due to low summer DO and high temperatures.
claims.qualification: Warmwater-focus NEVER implies trout are biologically absent — it records what the agency documents as the fishery. A couple of stray trout (e.g., Fishbrain rows) would be research leads, not fishery documentation.

source.title: TWRA Cherokee Reservoir where-to-fish page — summer stratification
source.pinpoint: "The reservoir thermally stratifies in the summer when warm oxygenated surface water cannot mix with the cold water below."; "oxygen levels below 30 ft. can become too low to support most fish species." Verified live 2026-09-22.

claims.statement: TWRA documents summer stratification with oxygen below 30 ft too low for most fish in many locations/summers — the physical reason no cold-water trout fishery is documented on this pool.
claims.qualification: Habitat context from the managing agency; temperature alone would never establish occupancy, and this documents unsuitability of the summer deep water rather than fish absence.

claims.statement: No trout program documents any stocking in the lake itself; whether individual trout ever occur in the pool is unknown.
claims.qualification: Absence of stocking rows and of fishery text is NOT proof trout are absent — recorded as unresolved, never as 'no trout'.

waters.unresolvedQuestion: Whether any trout occur in Cherokee Lake at all (no stocking program, no fishery documentation, no survey observation — absence unprovable, presence undocumented).
qualifications: Warmwater-focus is a documentation statement, not a biological absence claim.

The nearest documented trout water is the Cherokee Dam TAILWATER ~20 miles below the dam on the Holston River (catalog holston-river, Nov-Apr stocking, 'limited year-round fishing') — it is a different water and never transfers to the lake.
Even the striped-bass fishery here is documented as DO-limited in summer; the lake is a warmwater/coolwater system, not a trout refuge.

priorLeads.segment: Cherokee Lake (Cherokee Reservoir), the TVA impoundment of the Holston River across Grainger, Hamblen, Hawkins, and Jefferson counties northeast of Knoxville, impounded at its southwest end by Cherokee Dam. TWRA's fishery description covers the 30,300-surface-acre pool itself.

coldSourceSummary.notes: Full-pool contour 1,075 ft per TWRA's Cherokee Reservoir page ('TVA owns up to the 1,075-ft...'). TWRA: 'The reservoir thermally stratifies in the summer when warm oxygenated surface water cannot mix with the cold [deeper water]... During most summers and in many locations, oxygen levels below 30 ft. can become too low to support most fish species.' On-lake TDEC profile station TDECWPC-HOLST093.5HSS/HOLST093.5HSB 'CHEROKEE LAKE NEAR JOHNSON HOLLOW' (HUC 06010104) recorded 27.0 C surface / 24.4 C bottom on 2000-08-09. holdover.detail: Not applicable as a trout question - no trout fishery is documented for the reservoir. TWRA notes even the coldwater-striped-bass program is marginal here: stripers 'must be maintained by stocking' and 'do not normally grow big in Cherokee Reservoir, due to low summer dissolved [oxygen]'.

wildPopulation.detail: No trout population of any kind documented. TWRA's Cherokee Reservoir 'What you can catch' page lists Largemouth, Smallmouth, Striped, Cherokee (striper x white hybrid) bass, Crappie, Walleye, Saugeye, Paddlefish, White Bass, Bluegill, Catfish - no trout species appear anywhere in the fishery text (the only 'trout' strings on the page are navigation-menu items).

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: TWRA documents a warmwater fishery with no trout; the lake thermally stratifies each summer with 27 C surface water (TDEC on-lake profile, Aug 2000) and oxygen below 30 ft too low for most fish in most summers, and Cherokee is absent from TWRA's year-round reservoir trout stocking list while eight other reservoirs are on it.

waters.name: Chilhowee Lake

catalogFields.notes: Reservoir on the Little Tennessee River in Blount County below the Chilhowee Mountains, impounded by Chilhowee Dam. Receives the Little Tennessee River from Calderwood Lake and discharges into Tellico Lake. TWRA stocks the reservoir with rainbow trout in February, November, and December. TWRA maps the reservoir at 1,738 ac. TWRA's Chilhowee Reservoir page lists the fishery as largemouth bass, smallmouth bass, spotted bass, crappie, bluegill, catfish (see officialSources). The live trout list carries rainbow trout while an older plan snapshot differs; use the live list with the dated conflict noted in the source record.

waters.name: Citico Creek

catalogFields.notes:
Cherokee National Forest creek with TWRA stocking roughly February–July (the Forest Service's catchable-rainbow window upstream of Little Citico runs March 15–September 15) and wild brown, rainbow, and brook trout in the tributaries. Remote, brushy, rain-flashy.

Regulations: Tellico-Citico Permit Area "from Little Citico Creek confluence upstream to the North/South Fork junction": permit required Mar 1–Aug 15; closed Thu & Fri (holidays excepted); creel 7 trout, no size limit; one rod; sunrise–sunset fishing only (retrieved 2026-09-14; verify current rules with TWRA before you go).

headline.reachScope: Stocked main stem (Tellico-Citico permit area) vs wild-brook headwater tributary (Falls Branch)
headline.statement: TWRA stocks Citico Creek's main stem weekly through the Tellico-Citico program (22 consecutive 2026 weeks, Feb 22 - Jul 19) with a Tellico-Citico permit required Mar 1 - Aug 15; a headwater tributary (Falls Branch) holds a documented wild brook trout population - a seasonal stocked fishery plus wild headwaters, not a single year-round stocked fishery.

priorLeads.segment: Citico Creek main stem, Monroe County, in the Cherokee National Forest, flowing north to Tellico Lake (Little Tennessee HUC 06010204). The catalog covers both the stocked main stem and the wild-trout headwater forks. TWRA's Tellico-Citico Permit Area regulates the creek from its confluence with Little Citico Creek upstream to the confluence of the North and South Forks; the North/South Fork headwaters (incl. Falls Branch, a South Fork tributary) hold the documented wild brook trout.
priorLeads.boundaries: Permitted reach: Little Citico Creek confluence upstream to the North/South Fork junction (TWRA trout regulations page). Stocked reach is the main stem; wild trout are documented in the forks above.

coldSourceSummary.notes: Elevation figure applies to the headwaters, not the main stem: the TWRA Trout Management Plan 2017-2027 places Goat Falls on North Fork Citico Creek 'at ~3,200' (brook trout habitat discussion) - https://www.tn.gov/content/dam/tn/twra/documents/fishing/Tennessee-Trout-Management-Plan-2017-2027.pdf . The plan also describes the watershed as steep, remote, rain-flashy Cherokee NF terrain. No dam on the creek; cold source is forested mountain headwater elevation.

holdover.detail: No site-specific holdover study found. The main stem receives 22 consecutive weekly TWRA seasonal stockings (weeks of 2/22 through 7/19 in the 2026 schedule) and the permit area remains open to daily fishing Aug 16 - end of February without a permit, which implies fish availability into fall/winter, but no creel or tag-return evidence of holdover was located.

wildPopulation.detail: TWRA's Trout Management Plan 2017-2027 documents that until recently two streams in the Citico Creek watershed supported brook trout - upper North Fork Citico Creek and Falls Branch (South Fork Citico tributary); a 2013 distribution survey found only the Falls Branch population remains (naturalized, hatchery origin per 1990s genetics), with North Fork Citico extirpated above Goat Falls. USFS Cherokee NF states 'Wild trout, rainbow, brown and native brookies are present in most of the mountain streams above 1000 feet' (general CNF statement, not Citico-specific). The stocked main stem itself is not a wild trout water and is NOT on TWRA's Wild Trout Streams list.

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: A naturalized brook trout population persisted in the watershed (Falls Branch, 2013 TWRA survey) - documented year-round survival in the headwaters - while the stocked main stem showed ~23 C grab temperatures in June 2014 near its mouth, consistent with its put-grow-take role rather than fail.

waters.name: Clinch River (Norris tailwater)

catalogFields.notes:
One of the East’s classic tailwaters: big sulphur hatches, special-regulation trophy water below Norris Dam, and a famous mid-river sandbar flats scene. Flow is TVA-driven; the gauge below the dam is the wade-window truth-teller. The tailwater runs from Norris Dam through Melton Hill Lake down to the Clinch mouth at Kingston / Watts Bar Lake.

Regulations: Norris Dam downstream to Hwy 61 bridge (incl. tributaries): 14–20 in PLR on all trout; 7-trout creel, only 1 over 20 in (retrieved 2026-09-14; verify current rules with TWRA before you go).

headline.reachScope: Clinch River below Norris Dam (Norris Tailwater), Anderson County — approximately 14 miles from Norris Dam to the Hwy 61 Bridge at Clinton; downstream of Hwy 61 the river impounds into Melton Hill Lake (separate catalog water)

coldSourceSummary.notes: Freestone river draining the Cohutta Mountains through the Cherokee National Forest; the Tennessee scenic segment is a narrow valley run with Class II-III rapids per TDEC's paddling description. No dam, no spring-influence documentation for the TN reach. Gauge altitude at the US-411 boundary is ~756 ft (USGS 02384000), so the TN reach is low-elevation; no agency statement on TN-reach summer cold-water refuge was located.

holdover.detail: No trout presence of any kind documented for the Tennessee reach — no stocking program rows, no trout designation, no creel or angler documentation located — so holdover cannot be assessed.

wildPopulation.detail: No wild trout documented in the Tennessee reach. TDEC's Scenic River page describes a rich native fish community — 'more than 90 fish species and 25 mussel species' with federal and state-listed aquatic species — and names no trout. The celebrated rare-fish work and any trout headwater fishery (Cohutta Wilderness, Jacks River, GA's 2015 ONRW designation) are on the Georgia reaches and do not transfer to the TN reach. TWRA's stocking workbook contains zero Conasauga rows, and the river is absent from TWRA's wild-trout/special-regulation lists.

priorLeads.segment: Doe Creek (GNIS 01328063), a tributary of Roan Creek in Johnson County, TN (HUC 06010103 Watauga) that joins Roan Creek near Doeville. This is NOT the Doe River of Carter County (a separate catalog entry evidenced in batch 3). Identity verified via WQP station metadata: TDEC stations named 'Doe Creek' with CountyCode 091 (Johnson) and HUCEightDigitCode 06010103, spanning river-mile ~1.2 (36.3831,-81.9561) to river-mile ~7.6 (36.4344,-81.9139). USGS's own monitoring-location identity service was persistently 503 this week, so station name/county/HUC columns in the WQP CSV were used.
priorLeads.boundaries: Catalog gives no reach limits and TWRA stocks it countywide as 'Doe Creek'. Record covers the main stem from the upper TDEC station (RM 7.6 near Little Doe) to the mouth at Roan Creek near Doeville; eRegulations' walleye-run reach is 'Old Cabin Private Road downstream to Roan Creek'.

coldSourceSummary.notes: Free-flowing mountain tributary in the Watauga HUC (06010103); TDEC's Jan 2002 grab at RM 7.6 read 8.16 C and at RM 1.2 read 4.34 C, consistent with a cold upland stream. Corroborating agency context (not trout-specific): the creek's lower reach is one of the few Region 4 waters TWRA/eRegulations protect with a Jan 1-Apr 30 one-hook walleye-run restriction ('Doe Creek (Old Cabin Private Road downstream to Roan Creek)'), a restriction TWRA applies to cold spawning-run tributaries of Watauga Lake country. No gorge/canopy citation found.

holdover.detail: No holdover-specific creel or angler-verified documentation found for Doe Creek. A documented wild trout population (below) necessarily implies multi-season in-stream survival, but over-summer survival of stocked fish specifically is not separately documented.

wildPopulation.detail: TWRA Fisheries Report 18-01 (Region IV Trout Fisheries Report 2017): 'Some stocked steams (e.g., Beaverdam Creek, Doe Creek, Laurel Fork, and Doe River) do support excellent wild trout populations as well.' In that report's Johnson County context 'Doe Creek' is this Roan Creek tributary (the batch-3 Doe River record flagged the same sentence and explicitly identified its 'Doe Creek' as the Johnson County water). The report further characterizes the creek as one of the region's productive wild trout streams alongside its seasonal hatchery-supported fishery. Species composition of the wild component is not stated in the cited sentence. Note: the creek is NOT on TWRA's current Wild Trout Streams special-regulation list (that list's only Johnson County entry is Beaverdam Creek), so the wild fishery runs under statewide trout rules.

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: TWRA's own Region IV Trout Fisheries Report 2017 documents an excellent wild trout population in this exact creek - wild reproduction requires year-round in-stream survival - and TDEC grab samples 2001-2026 show summer peaks of only 14.9-18.2 C.

waters.name: Doe River

catalogFields.notes:

waters.name: Douglas Lake

catalogFields.notes:
TVA reservoir on the French Broad River east of Knoxville across Cocke, Jefferson, Sevier, and Hamblen counties, impounded by Douglas Dam (USGS 03468510 tailwater gauge, 35.96120/-83.53878). Receives the French Broad River and the Pigeon River; discharges through the dam into the French Broad tailwater toward the Holston/French Broad confluence. TWRA maps the reservoir at 28,738 ac. Aliases: Douglas Reservoir. TWRA's Douglas Reservoir page lists the fishery as largemouth bass, smallmouth bass, spotted bass, crappie, bluegill, catfish, striped bass (see officialSources). Striped bass is a regulatory or hybrid-evidence tag here; reservoir temperature/oxygen refuge context is not a scored input.

Regulations: black bass 5/day; Oct 1–May 31 no length limit; Jun 1–Sep 30 only one LMB/SMB >16 in/day; crappie 15/day, 10-in min; catfish 1/day >34 in; white/striped/hybrid 15/day; walleye+sauger 5/day combined, walleye 15-in min; muskellunge 1/day 36-in min; (retrieved 2026-09-14; verify current rules with TWRA before you go).

priorLeads.segment: Douglas Lake (TVA Douglas Reservoir) — the TVA impoundment of the French Broad River east of Knoxville across Cocke, Jefferson, Sevier and Hamblen counties, impounded by Douglas Dam (USGS 03468510 tailwater gauge at the dam, Sevier County). Receives the French Broad River and the Pigeon River; discharges through the dam into the French Broad tailwater. Sibling of the cataloged french-broad-river tailwater, which batch 1 documented as a warmwater control — this record addresses the LAKE itself with lake-specific evidence.
priorLeads.boundaries: Entire reservoir; TWRA full-pool harvest-restriction boundary extends up the Nolichucky to ENKA Dam, up the Pigeon to the Hwy 321 bridge at Newport, and up the French Broad to the Hwy 321 bridge. 30,600 acres, 555 miles of shoreline (TWRA); summer pool 1,000 ft with winter drawdown to ~940 ft.

coldSourceSummary.notes: TWRA describes Douglas as 'a fertile, Tennessee Valley Authority reservoir' whose pool 'can fluctuate 60 feet from the summer elevation of 1000 feet above sea level to the winter elevation of 940 feet', with 'thermal stratification... common during the summer months' and 'low dissolved oxygen concentrations... common during the summer' — a warm, fertile tributary impoundment, not a cold hypolimnetic-release body. No TVA release-depth specification is machine-verifiable (tva.com blocks automated fetch). Angling context per TWRA: in summer, fish hold below the thermocline and fishing is 'at depths of less than 10 feet (above the thermocline)'.

holdover.detail: No trout are stocked in the reservoir — the owner-supplied 2026 TWRA schedule (live feed re-verified 2026-09-18) contains zero 'Douglas' trout rows — and TWRA's reservoir page documents supplemental stocking only for sauger/walleye ('hatchery-reared fish are stocked if numbers become low'). There is no stocked-trout population to hold over; the same finding was made for the tailwater reach in the batch 1 french-broad-river control record.

wildPopulation.detail: No trout in TWRA's reservoir species account (largemouth bass 'one of the best largemouth bass fisheries in east Tennessee', 'best crappie reservoir in East Tennessee', bluegill, catfish, smallmouth, spotted bass, sauger/walleye, white bass); the reservoir has no entry on TWRA's wild trout or delayed-harvest lists.

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: Lake-specific evidence matches the tailwater control: zero TWRA trout stocking rows, a TWRA species account with no trout, and USGS grab samples at the dam (03468510) showing release water climbing to 26.5-27.0 C by August-September (1975-1980) in a reservoir TWRA documents as summer-stratified with low dissolved oxygen.

priorLeads.boundaries: Catalog covers the mainstem below the forks (hydroIdentity HUC8 08010202, GNIS 01306450). No USGS gage sits on this mainstem reach; nearest gaged reaches are the South Fork near Gates and at Chestnut Bluff (07027800, 07028000, Lauderdale County) and the North Fork at Dyersburg (07029100, Dyer County), all identified via the USGS statewide site file.

coldSourceSummary.notes: No gage and no dam/spring evidence was found for the mainstem reach itself; elevation and temperature left null rather than borrowed from the forks. USGS WRIR 92-4146 (Bailey 1993) places the forks: the 136-square-mile Jackson study area 'is between the Middle Fork Forked Deer and South Fork Forked Deer Rivers'.

holdover.detail: No trout documentation of any kind on the Forked Deer system. The river is absent from TWRA's live trout stocking list (checked 2026-09-18) and from the TWRA Trout Management Plan 2017-2027 (zero mentions of 'Forked Deer'); the plan states hatchery-supported waters 'are primarily warmwater habitats that cannot support trout year round'.

wildPopulation.detail: No wild trout documented anywhere on the Forked Deer system; TWRA's plan and stocking list contain no reference, and TWRA regulates the river under warmwater species rules ('Forked Deer, Hatchie, Loosahatchie, Obion, and Wolf Rivers (includes tributaries) - Crappie: 30 per day, no length limit').

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: Ungaged warmwater lowland mainstem, but every nearby gaged fork in the same system shows summer water temperatures of 27.0-32.0 C (USGS grab samples) and TWRA lists no trout program on any Forked Deer reach.

waters.name: Fort Loudoun Lake

catalogFields.notes: TVA reservoir at Knoxville across Knox, Blount, and Loudon counties, impounded by Fort Loudoun Dam (USGS 03499510 tailwater gauge, 35.79174/-84.24325; Tennessee River mile 602.3). Formed by the Holston and French Broad main stems and the Little Tennessee arm (Tellico Lake joins via the canal); discharges into Watts Bar Lake. TVA lists the reservoir at 14,600 ac at normal summer pool. Aliases: Fort Loudoun Reservoir. TWRA's Fort Loudoun Reservoir page lists the fishery as largemouth bass, smallmouth bass, spotted bass, crappie, bluegill, catfish, striped bass (see officialSources). priorLeads.segment: Fort Loudoun Lake (Fort Loudoun Reservoir), the 14,600-acre mainstem Tennessee River reservoir created by TVA's Fort Loudoun Dam in 1943 at Knoxville, spanning Knox, Blount, and Loudon counties and extending 55 miles upstream from the dam to the confluence of the Holston and French Broad rivers (Little Tennessee/Tellico arm joins via the canal).
priorLeads.boundaries: Entire pool: Fort Loudoun Dam (Tennessee River mile 602.3; USGS tailwater station 03499510 at 35.79174,-84.24325) upstream 55 miles to the Holston/French Broad confluence; discharges via lock and mainstem to Watts Bar Reservoir.

coldSourceSummary.notes: TWRA: 'Fort Loudoun contains 14,600 acres and was created by the Tennessee Valley Authority in 1943'; it is 'a navigable mainstream waterway' with only a six-foot annual drawdown (pool fluctuating 807-813 ft) — a low-storage run-of-river mainstem pool, the opposite of a deep cold-release storage reservoir. No agency page states a release type; the historical record measured in the dam's own tailwater (USGS 03499510, 1975-1979) shows summer release temperatures of 19-27 C, empirically confirming no cold bottom-draw regime.

holdover.detail: No trout presence to hold over: TWRA's Fort Loudoun fishery profile lists largemouth/smallmouth/white bass, bluegill, crappie, and catfish with zero trout content, Fort Loudoun appears nowhere in TWRA's 2026 trout stocking workbook, and the STMP's list of the nine Tennessee reservoirs that maintain year-round cold, well-oxygenated water and support trout fisheries does not include it.

wildPopulation.detail: No wild trout documentation. Fort Loudoun is absent from the STMP wild trout waters list, and no trout record exists for the reservoir in TWRA materials (catalog targetSpecies are bass/crappie/panfish/catfish/striped bass, consistent with TWRA's profile).

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: A shallow navigable mainstem Tennessee River pool (807-813 ft, six-foot drawdown) with documented summer temperatures of 20.6-27.0 C in the reservoir (TDEC 2011-2026) and 19-27 C in its own dam tailwater (USGS 03499510, 1975-1979), zero trout stocking rows, and no trout content in TWRA's fishery profile — excluded from the STMP's nine cold-water trout reservoirs.

waters.name: Fort Patrick Henry Lake

catalogFields.notes:
Small (~860 acre) TVA reservoir on the South Fork Holston River at Kingsport (Sullivan County), impounded by Fort Patrick Henry Dam (USGS 03487010, 36.49816/-82.50904). Receives the Boone tailwater (boone-tailwater) at its upper arm and discharges through the dam into the Fort Patrick Henry tailwater (ft-patrick-henry-tailwater), which joins the North Fork Holston River to form the Holston main stem at Kingsport. Aliases: FPH Lake, Fort Patrick Henry Reservoir. TWRA's Fort Patrick Henry Reservoir page lists the fishery as largemouth bass, smallmouth bass, spotted bass, crappie, bluegill, catfish, striped bass (see officialSources). Striped bass is a regulatory or hybrid-evidence tag here; reservoir temperature/oxygen refuge context is not a scored input.

Stocked trout fishery documented by agency sources in the 2026-09 wave-ledger sourcing pass (retrieved 2026-09-14) — TMP nine-trout-reservoir list ("Region IV, Fort Patrick Henry — Brown and Rainbow"); stocking months unpinned.

Regulations: reservoir table (statewide otherwise): LM 5/day no length, SM 15-in min; spotted 15/day; crappie 15/day 10-in; catfish ≤34-in unlimited, one >34-in/day; striped/hybrid 2/day 15-in; walleye 5/day 18-in. Trout: statewide 7/day, no length limit; (retrieved 2026-09-14; verify current rules with TWRA before you go).

priorLeads.boundaries: Full named length per catalog ('runs its full named length down toward the upper Clinch' drainage). coldSourceSummary.notes: No dam anywhere on the creek. The stream drains the Cumberland Gap notch of Cumberland Mountain through a protected park corridor (NPS monitoring stations sit inside Cumberland Gap NHP), which gives the upper reach permanent riparian cover; the 1,300-ft gap elevation context is inferred from the USGS station name 'AT CUMBERLAND GAP' only — no agency elevation figure captured. wildPopulation.detail: No wild trout record found for Gap Creek (Claiborne). The TWRA Trout Management Plan 2017-2027 wild trout stream list does not include it (plan text searched; 'Gap Creek' appears only in an unrelated GSMNP context), and the STMP class statement describes hatchery-supported streams as primarily warmwater. NPS fish-community documentation for the park's Gap Creek was not located in this pass.

waters.name: Hiwassee River (Appalachia tailwater / Reliance)

catalogFields.notes:
The Southeast’s big tailwater: TWRA-managed delayed-harvest-free trophy water with wild-strength rainbow, brown and some brook trout, and famous summer evening hatches (White Fly, Yellow Sally). A winter catch-and-release season (Oct 1–Feb 28) keeps the river fishable all year. Two- and four-turbine releases swing flow hard — the Reliance gauge is the call. The tailwater runs from the Appalachia Dam release water at the NC line through Reliance to the Chickamauga Lake head.

Regulations: Appalachia Powerhouse downstream to L&N Railroad Bridge: Mar 1–Sep 30 — 7-trout creel, only 2 may be brown trout; Catch-and-Release season Oct 1–Feb 28 (artificial lures only, no harvest/possession) (retrieved 2026-09-14; verify current rules with TWRA before you go).

headline.reachScope: Hiwassee tailwater trout water from Apalachia Powerhouse to Patty Bridge Access (~17 miles; most productive 5 miles Powerhouse to Reliance). The ~8 miles of riverbed between Apalachia Dam and the powerhouse are bypassed by pipeline and are not the trout water.
headline.statement: TWRA documents year-round stocked trout fishing on the Hiwassee tailwater, but explicitly as 'limited year-round fishing': elevated summer water temperatures prevent many trout from holding over, so the year-round label carries a real summer limitation.

priorLeads.segment: Holston River MAIN STEM from the North/South Fork confluence at Kingsport through Hawkins, Grainger, Jefferson, and Knox counties to the French Broad confluence at the head of Fort Loudoun Lake (catalog boundaries). The documented trout fact set sits entirely on the Cherokee Dam tailwater sub-reach of this main stem (Jefferson/Grainger counties); South Fork Holston tailwaters and North Fork Holston are separate catalog waters.
priorLeads.boundaries: Kingsport (fork confluence) to French Broad confluence; TWRA's smallmouth exception manages 'I-40 bridge upstream to Cherokee Dam' on this main stem; the stocking program is reach-pinned to 'Cherokee TW / Holston River' (Jefferson/Grainger).

coldSourceSummary.notes: TWRA Trout Management Plan 2017-2027 (Fisheries Report 17-10): 'The Cherokee and Apalachia tailwaters also have summer thermal bottlenecks (with water temperatures >70 F) and receive adult Rainbow and Brown Trout during the fall and spring' — an agency-documented summer thermal ceiling on this tailwater, and a seasonally (not year-round) cold regime. TDEC's 2026 303(d) list records a 26.9-mile Holston River segment in Jefferson County (unit TN06010104001_2000) impaired for DISSOLVED OXYGEN with source 'DAM OR IMPOUNDMENT' (plus FLOW REGIME MODIFICATION, dam-sourced) — the dam-release water-quality signature on the Cherokee-Dam-downstream reach; the 303(d) sheet prints unit IDs and miles but not boundary text, so reach attribution rests on the dam-sourced source field and Jefferson County location. Release draw level (bottom-draw vs epilimnion) is not documented in any source retrieved; TVA's Cherokee page could not be fetched (blocked). Gauge note: USGS 03493510 'HOLSTON RIVER AT CHEROKEE DAM(TW), TN' (Jefferson Co., HUC 06010104, drainage 3,428 sq mi) is a discontinued discrete-sampling site, and no active USGS gauge reports on the Holston main stem in Tennessee.

holdover.detail: No holdover or year-round survival documentation found for the Cherokee tailwater reach. TWRA's own plan designs this as a seasonal fishery: adult trout stocked fall and spring around a documented >70 F summer thermal bottleneck; STMP documents significant natural brown trout reproduction only for the South Holston and Wilbur tailwaters, not Cherokee.

wildPopulation.detail: No wild trout population documented on the Holston main stem / Cherokee tailwater. The STMP statement that significant natural brown trout reproduction enables wild management applies only to the South Holston and Wilbur tailwaters ('no Brown Trout are stocked' there — unlike Cherokee, which receives adult Browns).

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: Owner-box conflict, stated both sides: the site feed (repo trout-calendar.json) claims 'No trout program (warmwater fishery)' and the owner-supplied workbook row 'Cherokee TW / Holston River' carries NO stocking months, while the catalog YAML claims a Nov-Apr program and TWRA's LIVE 2026 schedule (fetched 2026-09-18) confirms the row WITH months 'J, F, M, A, N, D' (Rainbow + Brown) — and TWRA's own plan documents >70 F summer thermal bottlenecks on this tailwater, i.e., a documented seasonal fishery rather than documented year-round survival.

waters.name: Little Tennessee River

catalogFields.notes:
Main-stem river entering Tennessee from North Carolina below Fontana Dam, flowing through the Calderwood and Chilhowee pools and Tellico Lake (impounded reaches are carried by the lake features; no tailwater condition scoring is applied across a reservoir) to its mouth at the Tennessee River in Fort Loudoun Lake below Tellico Dam. The 33-mile dam-to-dam corridor is the Little T of TVA's main- stem sequence; the trout-stocked upper water is the reach below Chilhowee Dam — verify current TWRA schedules. Distinct from the Tellico River (tellico-river), a different tributary near Tellico Plains. USGS 03519750 (Little Tennessee River at Davis Ferry) sits mid-pool.

Stocked trout fishery confirmed by agency sources (retrieved 2026-09-14) — Trout water is the Chilhowee-tailwater reach (upper Little Tennessee arm); late-winter/early-spring rainbow plants per TWRA.

Regulations: Tellico Lake Chota Refuge Unit (Little Tennessee River Miles 26.0 upstream to 29.7) closed to all forms of use and trespass Nov 15–Feb 28 except in designated observation areas (retrieved 2026-09-14; verify current rules with TWRA before you go).

waters.name: Nickajack Lake

catalogFields.notes:
Tennessee River impoundment from Nickajack Dam (USGS 03570525 tailwater gauge) upstream 46 miles through Chattanooga to Chickamauga Dam (Marion/Hamilton counties). Downstream of Chickamauga Lake; below the dam the main stem continues toward Guntersville Lake in Alabama as tennessee-river. TVA lists the reservoir at about 10,700 acres — a scenic gorge reach below the dam and a wide, urban Chattanooga reach above it. Verify TVA release schedules before paddling the gorge. TWRA's Nickajack Reservoir page lists the fishery as largemouth bass, smallmouth bass, spotted bass, crappie, bluegill, catfish, striped bass (see officialSources).
Striped bass is a regulatory or hybrid-evidence tag here; reservoir temperature/oxygen refuge context is not a scored input.

Regulations: black bass 5/day in combination; largemouth 15-in min; smallmouth/spotted/Alabama no minimum, only one over 16 in/day; crappie 15/day 10-in min; catfish no creel ≤34 in, one >34 in/day; striped/hybrid 2/day 15-in min; white bass 15/day; walleye 5/day 16-in; (retrieved 2026-09-14; verify current rules with TWRA before you go).

priorLeads.segment: Nickajack Lake / Nickajack Reservoir — the TVA mainstem Tennessee River impoundment formed by Nickajack Dam (at Tennessee River mile 427.7, near New Hope in Marion County, impounded 1967) and backing 46 miles upstream through Chattanooga to Chickamauga Dam (catalog: Marion/Hamilton counties). TWRA documents the fishery entirely as warmwater: largemouth/smallmouth/spotted bass, crappie, bluegill/redear, catfish, white/striped/hybrid bass, sauger, walleye, paddlefish — 'no mention of trout or trout stocking anywhere on this page'. At full summer pool it covers 10,370 acres with 192 miles of shoreline (TWRA). The USGS tailwater gauge at the dam is 03570525 'TENNESSEE RIVER AT NICKAJACK DAM (TAILWATER), TN'.

coldSourceSummary.notes: Mainstem run-of-river reservoir: TVA operates Nickajack near a constant full pool (~633.5-634 ft) with a short retention time of roughly 3-4 days, so the impoundment tracks mainstem Tennessee River temperature rather than behaving like a cold deep-release storage project; no selective cold-water withdrawal regime is documented for the dam. The tailwater gauge record (below) shows warm releases. elevationFt = full pool per TVA data (~633.5-634 ft; TVA land-plan summary ~10,200 acres vs TWRA's 10,370).

holdover.detail: No trout fishery of any kind is documented: zero Nickajack rows in TWRA's 2026 trout stocking workbook, the reservoir is absent from the TWRA Trout Management Plan's list of the nine Tennessee reservoirs that support trout fisheries (Dale Hollow, Parksville, South Holston, Wilbur, Watauga, Fort Patrick Henry, Calderwood, Chilhowee, Tellico), and TWRA's Nickajack Reservoir page lists no trout and no holdover fishery.

wildPopulation.detail: No wild trout documented. TWRA's species list for the reservoir is entirely warmwater (bass, crappie, sunfish, catfish, striped/hybrid bass, sauger/walleye, paddlefish), and the Trout Management Plan's wild-trout discussion limits wild trout to East Tennessee mountain streams with no mention of Nickajack.

waters.name: Nolichucky River

catalogFields.notes:
Freestone river draining NC mountains — clear and cold in spring, warm by August. TWRA’s stocking dataset does not currently list it; upstream reaches hold scattered wild fish. Rain-flashy; the Embreeville gauge matters. It runs from the NC line to its Douglas Lake confluence. TWRA's statewide regulation exceptions set a smallmouth bass rule on this water: 13–17 in protected length range, one over 17 in per day. (see officialSources).

Regulations: Black Bass 5/day in combination; Smallmouth 13–17 in PLR, only 1 over 17 in/day ("ENKA Dam upstream to the state line includes Davy Crockett Lake"); lower reach under Douglas Reservoir rules to ENKA Dam (retrieved 2026-09-14; verify current rules with TWRA before you go).

priorLeads.segment: The full Tennessee main stem of the Nolichucky River from the NC state line to its Douglas Lake confluence (catalog boundaries). Facts below are attributed by reach: the USGS gauge and temperature record are at Embreeville (Washington County agricultural valley, 805 sq mi drainage), NOT the upstream Erwin gorge; TDEC's 303(d) agricultural impairments sit on the Greene/Washington County middle reaches; trout evidence in agency sources is tributary-level (Nolichucky-watershed headwater streams), not main stem.

coldSourceSummary.notes: Freestone, undammed main stem (no dam or release-type record exists for this water). holdover.detail: No holdover documentation found; there is no stocking program to hold over fish and no creel or study record for this river was located.

wildPopulation.detail: Main-stem wild trout presence: unknown. The catalog claims 'upstream reaches hold scattered wild fish' but no agency source located documents trout in the Nolichucky main stem. What agency sources DO document is tributary-level: the TWRA Trout Management Plan's brook-restoration table lists Nolichucky-watershed headwater streams with resident trout (Phillips Hollow 'RBT/BKT', Devil Fork 'RBT', Jennings Creek 'hatchery-influenced Brook Trout population') and states native brook restoration 'would establish native Brook Trout populations in the Nolichucky watershed (where none exist)' — brook trout absent watershed-wide, and all named trout populations are small headwater tributaries, not the river.

priorLeads.segment: Normandy Reservoir, the TVA impoundment of the Duck River headwaters upstream of Normandy Dam (Bedford/Coffee County line near Normandy and Manchester). This is the lake itself; the duck-river-tailwater catalog entry (a separate water, evidenced in batch 1) begins below the dam.

coldSourceSummary.notes: Full summer pool 875 ft MSL (winter pool 864 ft), per TVA lake information. A eutrophic tributary reservoir per the Tennessee 305(b) reporting cited by EPA NEPIS archives - warm, productive basin, not a cold deep-release storage reservoir in the South Holston/Watauga sense.

holdover.detail: No trout holdover evidence exists or is expected to be documented: TWRA's Normandy Reservoir fishing page documents a warmwater fishery (largemouth/smallmouth/spotted bass, crappie, bluegill, catfish, walleye) with no trout fishery, and the repo TWRA stocking workbook contains zero trout stocking rows for the reservoir. wildPopulation.detail: No wild trout presence documented anywhere for Normandy Reservoir. TWRA's page lists only warmwater gamefish; the Trout Management Plan places wild trout in East Tennessee mountain streams, not Middle Tennessee impoundments.

waters.name: Norris Lake

catalogFields.notes:
TVA reservoir on the Clinch River north of Knoxville across Anderson, Campbell, Claiborne, Grainger, and Union counties, impounded by Norris Dam (USGS 03533000 tailwater gauge). Receives the Clinch River and Powell River (powell-river); the dam releases the Clinch River Norris tailwater (clinch-river) into Melton Hill Lake. Aliases: Norris Reservoir. TVA's summer-normal full pool is about 33,840 acres, and the pool outline runs far up the Clinch and Powell arms — expect shorelines and access points to follow the impounded river channels. TWRA's Norris Reservoir page lists the fishery as largemouth bass, smallmouth bass, spotted bass, crappie, bluegill, catfish, striped bass (see officialSources).
Striped bass is a regulatory or hybrid-evidence tag here; reservoir temperature/oxygen refuge context is not a scored input.

Regulations: Smallmouth 1/day 18-in min Jun 1–Oct 15 (otherwise 5/day 15-in min, combined with largemouth 5/day, largemouth 14-in min); striped bass 2/day 15-in Apr 1–Oct 31, 1/day 36-in Nov 1–Mar 31; walleye/sauger 5/day 15-in from dam upstream to Grissom Island; (retrieved 2026-09-14; verify current rules with TWRA before you go).

waters.unresolvedQuestion: Whether any trout occur in Norris Lake (no stocking program, no fishery documentation, no verified observation — absence unprovable, presence undocumented).
qualifications: Warmwater-focus is a documentation statement, not a biological absence claim.
The documented trout water on this system is the Clinch River Norris TAILWATER below the dam (~14 miles to Hwy 61, catalog clinch-river) — dam-blocked from the lake and never transferring to it.
The lake's Clinch and Powell arms run far upstream; upper-arm habitat differs from the main pool — any future trout question must be arm-specific.

priorLeads.segment: Norris Lake (Norris Reservoir), the 34,200-acre TVA reservoir impounded by Norris Dam (completed 1936, the first TVA reservoir) on the Clinch River across Anderson, Campbell, Claiborne, Grainger, and Union counties. This record covers the RESERVOIR only; the cold-water trout fishery the dam creates is the Clinch River Norris tailwater below the dam (separate catalog entry), and TWRA's Norris stocking program content applies to that tailwater, not the lake.
priorLeads.boundaries: Entire pool from Norris Dam upstream along the Clinch arm (to the Virginia-line Clinch headwaters) and the Powell River arm (pool extends upstream to Gap Creek's confluence per TWRA's Powell River regulation boundary).

coldSourceSummary.notes: TWRA's Norris page states Norris 'was the first reservoir constructed by the Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA)' with the dam completed in 1936, impounding the Clinch and Powell rivers; primary purposes flood control and hydroelectric power. The dam's cold-release regime sustains the famous Norris TAILWATER trout fishery (STMP: Norris is among the heavily-fished stocked tailwaters with a 14-20 inch protected length limit and adult Brook Trout plants) — that fishery lies below the dam and is attributed to the clinch-river catalog entry, not this lake. Deep-main-lake summer cold-pool characteristics were not measured in this pass (the catalog notes reservoir temperature/oxygen refuge context is not a scored input); the documented lake temperatures here are warm upper-arm surface values.

holdover.detail: No trout holdover is documented because no trout fishery exists in the reservoir: TWRA's Norris page documents striped bass (~103,000 fingerlings/yr), walleye (~240,000/yr, mostly Lake Erie strain), and crappie (~103,000/yr) stocking plus black bass — with zero trout content anywhere in the fishery text. The only TWRA trout rows carrying the Norris name are 'Norris Tailwater / Clinch River' (Tailwater type, Rainbow+Brown+Brook, months M,A,M,J,J,A,S) — the river below the dam. The STMP's list of the nine Tennessee reservoirs that maintain year-round cold, well-oxygenated water and support trout fisheries (Dale Hollow, Parksville, South Holston, Wilbur, Watauga, Fort Patrick Henry, Calderwood, Chilhowee, Tellico) does not include Norris.

wildPopulation.detail: No wild trout documentation of any kind for the reservoir; Norris is absent from the STMP wild trout waters list, and tributary spawning attempts are described by the STMP as 'largely unsuccessful' in Tennessee reservoir trout programs generally.

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: TWRA's nine-reservoir list of Tennessee waters that maintain year-round cold, well-oxygenated water and support trout fisheries excludes Norris; TWRA's own Norris page documents an entirely warmwater fishery (striped bass, walleye, crappie, black bass; zero trout content), and TDEC measured 29.7-29.75 C surface water in the Clinch, Big Barren, and Powell arms in July 2022.

waters.name: Parksville Lake

catalogFields.notes:
Ocoee River impoundment (TVA Ocoee Dam No. 1, "Parksville Dam") in Polk County southeast of Benton; the dam sits at the pool's west edge. Receives the upper Ocoee River (ocoee-river) below Ocoee Number Three Lake and discharges through the dam into the Parksville tailwater (parksville-tailwater), which joins the Hiwassee River. TWRA lists the same pool as "Ocoee Lake" (2,112 ac). Aliases: Ocoee Lake, Ocoee Lake No. 1, Parksville Reservoir. TWRA's Parksville Reservoir page lists the fishery as largemouth bass, spotted bass, crappie, bluegill (see officialSources).

coldSourceSummary.notes: The catalog names Waterville (upstream generation driving the Hartford whitewater reach) but no agency page retrieved this session verifies the dam's operator or release draw (duke-energy and TDEC Pigeon River URLs 404'd; tva.com blocked in prior passes — the Pigeon is not a TVA reservoir). What TDEC's 2026 303(d) list DOES document is thermal: Cocke County assessment unit TN06010106001_4000 (5.03 mi) is impaired for TEMPERATURE (Low) with source 'DAM OR IMPOUNDMENT', plus FLOW REGIME MODIFICATION (dam), and COLOR from 'INDUSTRIAL POINT SOURCE DISCHARGE' and 'SOURCES OUTSIDE STATE JURISDICTION OR BORDERS' (the Canton NC paper mill signature) — the 303(d) extract prints unit IDs and miles but not boundary text; unit _4000 is the only dam-sourced Pigeon segment and the 5.03-mile length matches the Waterville-to-Hartford gorge, so the temperature impairment is attributable to the dam-regulated upper reach. This is a documented WARM-release (temperature non-support) signal, not evidence of cold tailwater. USGS station altitude at Newport is 1,038 ft; the gorge reach upstream is higher but no verified elevation figure was located.

priorLeads.segment: Reelfoot Lake — Tennessee's largest natural lake (10,427 acres), formed by the 1811-12 New Madrid earthquakes when the Mississippi ran backward into a shallow basin; roughly 68% is 3 feet deep or less. Spans Lake and Obion counties (plus Fulton Co., KY). TWRA documents it as one of the state's premier crappie and bluegill fisheries; trout are not mentioned anywhere on TWRA's lake page.
priorLeads.boundaries: Entire lake as cataloged. USGS lake gage 07027000 'REELFOOT LAKE NR TIPTONVILLE, TN' (36.3531,-89.4062, Lake County) monitors lake stage. TWRA page: US Fish and Wildlife Service oversees part of the lake (Kirby Pocket to Brewer's Bar); Reelfoot Lake State Park borders it. The only 'Reelfoot' trout row in TWRA's 2026 schedule — 'Union City Reelfoot Packing Site' (Obion Co., Winter rainbow) — is the separate Union City winter-trout pond cataloged as union-city-reelfoot-pond, NOT this lake.

coldSourceSummary.notes: Natural lake, no dam tailwater: TWRA describes it as created by the 1811-12 earthquakes. SpringFed=false basis: documented origin is river backwater filling a shallow surface basin (a runoff/bayou-fed lake, e.g. Running Reelfoot Bayou), not a spring system. elevationFt = USGS gage altitude 270.11 ft (NAVD88) at station 07027000, identity verified via waterservices expanded site output.

holdover.detail: No trout fishery of any kind is documented on the lake: no Reelfoot Lake row exists in TWRA's 2026 trout stocking schedule (the only 'Reelfoot' row is the separate Union City Packing Site pond), trout are absent from TWRA's lake page, and no holdover record exists. A WebSearch synthesis additionally characterizes the lake as hypereutrophic (EPA report lead, not fetched) — extreme summer warmth is consistent with the TDEC June samples (25.5-34.4 C).

wildPopulation.detail: No wild trout documented. priorLeads.segment: Lawrence County, TN main stem of Shoal Creek (GNIS 00153439, HUC 06030005 Pickwick Lake subbasin) - a large free-flowing Highland Rim stream flowing southwest from the Lawrenceburg area past David Crockett State Park to the Iron City area at the Alabama line, continuing to the Tennessee River at Florence AL (the Alabama reach is a different jurisdiction and is not covered here). Documented at two USGS stations on the TN reach: 03588000 Shoal Creek at Lawrenceburg (55.4 sq mi drainage) and 03588500 Shoal Creek at Iron City (348 sq mi drainage).
priorLeads.boundaries: Catalog gives no reach limits; record covers the TN main stem in Lawrence County from the Lawrenceburg area (~784 ft gauge datum) downstream to Iron City (~534 ft gauge datum) near the state line. All temperature facts below are from the two TN gauge stations.

coldSourceSummary.notes: Low-elevation Highland Rim stream: gauge datum 534.22 ft NGVD29 at Iron City (lower end of the TN reach) and 784.41 ft at Lawrenceburg (upper end), per WQP station metadata. David Crockett State Park (Lawrenceburg) sits on this creek west of town (park page describes the park as along Shoal Creek); the park page documents no trout fishery. Wave-2 ledger also flagged a second in-town station (03588000, discontinued daily record 1932-1991; WQP water-quality samples 1967-1991).

holdover.detail: No holdover documentation of any kind found, and no put-and-take basis on this water: TWRA's live 2026 stocking datatable (616 rows, fetched 2026-09-18) contains zero rows for a location named 'Shoal Creek' - the only Shoal token is 'East Fork Shoal Creek' (Lawrence Co.), a different catalog water. A 2005 Tuscaloosa News report describes historical TWRA stockings of ~1,000 trout into Shoal Creek (January and March) in a normal season, but this is a newspaper item, not an acceptable sole source, and no agency schedule confirms it; noted as a lead only.

wildPopulation.detail: No wild trout documentation found on any TN reach of Shoal Creek. Peer-reviewed survey of Factory Creek (Shoal Creek system, Pickwick Lake subbasin; 2017 collections, 58 species extant of 75 historical) documents a species-rich warmwater fish assemblage and names no trout. Shoal Creek appears on no TWRA wild trout, delayed-harvest, or special-regulation trout list; its regional reputation is a smallmouth/black bass stream.

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: USGS grab samples at the Iron City station (348 sq mi, representative of the whole TN reach below Lawrenceburg) show July-August water up to 28.0 C across 1974-2005, with the smaller upper station also reaching 26.5 C - warmwater summer conditions on a stream TWRA does not stock and where no trout are documented.
